landmarks.name: Butter Slip
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1616 and lined with butter stalls on market days — its shady steps kept the butter cool, and made the lane famously slippery.

landmarks.name: St Canice's
landmarks.blurb: Begun around 1202, it's Ireland's second-longest cathedral — and it gave the city its name: Cill Chainnigh, the Church of Canice.

landmarks.name: Round Tower
landmarks.blurb: Over 1,000 years old and 30 m tall — climb its 121 steps for the best view in Kilkenny. One of very few round towers in Ireland you can still climb.

landmarks.name: Smithwick's
landmarks.blurb: Franciscan friars brewed ale on this spot in the 1200s. John Smithwick started his brewery here in 1710 — quietly, since Catholics couldn't legally own property.

landmarks.name: St Mary's
landmarks.blurb: Built 1843–1857, right through the Great Famine, and paid for by local people. Its tower rises nearly 60 m over the city.

landmarks.name: Kilkenny Castle
landmarks.blurb: Home of the Butler family for almost 600 years — until 1967, when they sold it to the people of Kilkenny for just £50.
